newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen down amid sideways drift.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen down amid sideways drift.

text.p: Polish shares rose in higher turnover but analysts saw them slightly down on Tuesday within a near-term horizontal trend as the end of the year was likley to make some investors take profits and close positions.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.5 percent, to 13,743.8, and turnover rose 9.8 percent to 79.8 million zlotys ($28.6 million) on both markets as 53 issues rose, 12 fell and 18 were flat.

"It seems the market is not too strong, despite a good economic climate ... many investors want to take their profits and close positions before the end of the year," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said the 100-percent growth since the beginning of the year to an October 9th high of 15,078.7 points of the WIG index had cooled investor interest.
Some analysts said the market was likely to swing in a channel between 13,000 and 14,000 in the next two weeks and expected a rebound only at the beginning of next year or before Christmas.

They said Monday's news showing year-on-year GDP increasing in the third quarter of 1996 to 7.3 percent from 5.2 percent in the second quarter was a positive signal, but could have an impact on the bourse only in the long term.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.3 million zlotys ($0.5 million) with five stocks falling and one flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units were down one percent in a 23.6-million-zloty (8.4 million) turnover in regular session and fell 3.4 percent in 21.7-million zloty ($7.8 million) continuous trade.
